demoMerchantTask: Build meal deal listings, stock management, and order redemption.

stepThreeTitle: Follow the work. Step in anywhere.

privacySeoDescription: How {appName}, the agents you choose, and this website handle your information.
privacyIntro: This policy describes the current {appName} application and website. {appName} is an open source project operated by {operatorName}.
privacyLocalBody: The current version of {appName} runs on your device and stores the configuration and session data it manages locally. {appName} does not upload your code, conversations, or usage data to servers operated by {operatorName}.
privacyAgentsTitle: Agents and tools from other providers
privacyAgentsBody: {appName} starts the third-party coding agents you configure. These agents and their tools may send prompts, code, context, and other data to their service providers according to your configuration and actions. Their providers’ privacy policies and terms apply to that processing. Repository operations may also connect to the Git remotes you configure, including when checking remote status.
privacySharingBody: To coordinate work, task descriptions, reports, and relevant context pass between participating sessions. When this information enters another agent's session, it may be processed by that agent's configured provider. Working with agents from different providers may therefore involve sharing task information with multiple providers.
privacyWebsiteAnalyticsBody: This is a static website hosted on GitHub Pages. We use a cookie to remember the language selected or detected for this browser for one year. We use Google Analytics to understand website visits only if you allow it when this website asks; it then uses cookies and sends usage data to Google. If you decline, Google Analytics is not loaded. We remember your answer in a cookie for one year, and you can change it at any time with “Analytics settings” at the bottom of each page. GitHub records visitors' IP addresses for security purposes; see GitHub's privacy statement.
privacyContactTitle: Information you choose to send us
privacyContactBody: If you contact us by email or through GitHub Issues, we receive the information you choose to provide and use it to respond to your request. Information posted in a public issue is visible to others. For privacy questions, contact {operatorName} at the email address below.
privacyFutureBody: Remote host support is planned and is not an available feature. This policy does not describe it.

platformsSupportDescription: The macOS and Windows apps are in beta and are still in development. Linux support is planned as a server accessed from another machine’s browser. iOS and Android apps are also planned.
platformsWindowsInstall: On Windows, download the installer whose name ends in x64-setup.exe from a release. It needs Windows 10 version 21H2 or later, installs for your user account only, and downloads Microsoft Edge WebView2 if it is missing. On Windows 11 on Arm, the x64 app runs under emulation. The Windows app is not code-signed yet, so Microsoft Defender SmartScreen may show “Windows protected your PC”: select “More info”, then “Run anyway”.

faqSetupQuestion: Do I need to set up my projects and CLI configuration again?
faqSetupAnswer: Add your existing project folder without moving your code. The default account uses your existing CLI configuration, and the agent still loads your project's instructions, skills, hooks, and MCP servers. Additional accounts use separate configurations, with optional sharing of supported settings.
faqSubagentsQuestion: Why not develop every project in one session, or have one agent use subagents?
faqProvidersQuestion: Can each project keep an agent from a different provider?
faqParticipationQuestion: How do projects report back, and can I step in?
faqParticipationAnswer: A requirement or code detail may be easier to explain directly to the project agent doing the work. You can enter its conversation to add context, adjust requirements, or review code; sessions started by the coordinator still report results, open items, and decisions needed back to it.
developerTitle:
Let AI write the code.
Put your energy into the product.
developerIntro: I built {appName} because I believe people no longer need to write code by hand. Developers can put their attention back where it matters: the product they want to deliver.
developerShiftBody: As AI produces more code, reviewing and rewriting every line by hand can no longer keep pace. I see the shift toward implementation happening inside a black box as irreversible. In my view, AI already writes more complete logic than most programmers. The conventions for “good code” that we designed around human readers are losing their central role as AI takes on both writing and maintenance.
developerContextBody: I see the biggest obstacle in AI development as misunderstanding: unclear requirements, missing context, or assumptions left unstated. The work that deserves our attention is defining the problem, explaining constraints, and giving agents the context they need to work toward the same goal.
developerQualityBody: For me, software quality has one deciding standard: whether the product meets real needs under thorough testing. Reading code cannot establish that on its own. Tests need to cover real workflows, edge cases, and failures, and their results need to guide the next iteration.
developerPurpose: That is the purpose of this workspace: coordinating agents, carrying context forward, and following the work through to delivery. As developers spend less time in code editors, they can devote more of it to requirements, decisions, testing, and the product itself.
developerInvitation: If you also believe people no longer need to write code themselves, this workspace is built for you.

workspaceIntroduction: Bring your existing coding agents and accounts into one development workspace. Switch accounts within the same agent while keeping the conversation, or hand work to an agent from another provider. Choose an agent to coordinate tasks across your projects.
contextWindowFeatureDescription: Track context size and window usage, when reported by the agent, to see how close the conversation is to its context limit. Move the next stage to a fresh session before the conversation grows too long to reduce the risk of losing details during compression.
conversationRelayFeatureDescription: When a conversation gets too long, pass the remaining work to a fresh session. While the original agent still has the conversation record, you can revisit it or resume the old session to ask about earlier decisions and implementation details.
quotaRecoveryFeatureDescription: With automatic account switching enabled, a task stopped by its usage limit waits if no account of the same agent is available. Once a fresh usage reading confirms that an account has recovered, the system can resume the interrupted task.
teamCoordinationFeatureDescription: Let a coordinating agent assign work to other agents according to the task. The agents carry out their parts and exchange findings, then the coordinator brings the results together.
projectCoordinationFeatureDescription: Choose an agent to coordinate work across frontend, backend and other projects. It assigns tasks to their agents and follows progress and dependencies between projects.
separateProjectContextFeatureDescription: Each project runs in a separate session of its chosen agent and loads its own instructions and tool configuration, keeping different projects’ development context out of a single conversation.
existingWorkflowFeatureDescription: Add existing project folders without moving the code. Your agent’s CLI keeps loading the project’s instructions, Skills, Hooks and MCP configuration. Additional accounts can share selected settings from the default account.
coordinationWalkthroughDescription: Take a meal promotion across a restaurant’s ordering, payment and store-management projects. The illustration below shows a coordinator assigning tasks and receiving reports. Select a project to see its assigned task and example report.
faqSetupCostsAnswer: Install and configure the coding-agent command-line tools you want to use first. {appName} is free and open source under the MIT License; agents and model services follow the subscriptions or billing terms of the providers you choose. If your agent supports a self-hosted model, you can keep using that configuration too.
faqDataFlowAnswer: {appName} keeps its application data locally and does not upload your code or conversations to its own servers. Claude Code, Codex and Grok Build use services you subscribe to or configure, with your own accounts; these tools manage account credentials and conversation records. They send prompts, code and relevant context to the providers you configure, under those providers’ policies. When agents collaborate, task descriptions, progress and relevant context also pass to the agents taking part.
faqParallelWorkAnswer: Sessions share the project folder by default, so simultaneous edits to the same file can conflict. For parallel work, ask the agents to use separate Git worktrees and review the changes before merging.
faqCliResumeAnswer: Yes. Project files stay in their original folders and each agent keeps its own conversation records. While the original agent still has a conversation record, you can resume that conversation through its command-line tool. With an extra account, start the tool using that account’s configuration directory.
faqRemoteExecutionAnswer: Not yet. Running project agents on another server or computer is planned, but is not available.
privacyRemoteExecutionBody: Support for running agents on another server or computer is planned and is not available yet. This policy does not cover that feature.

faqProjectIsolationAnswer: Developing several projects in one session can mix their contexts. Working across directories or using subagents does not guarantee that the target project’s full configuration is loaded: rules can be missed when the parent session has to pass them on, and loading behavior varies by tool. {appName} starts an independent native session of the chosen agent in each project directory, so the agent loads local configuration through its own mechanisms while the coordinator organizes the work.
faqAgentChoiceAnswer: Yes. Choose Claude Code, Codex or Grok Build independently for the coordinator and each project, based on the task and the project’s tools. Each agent keeps its own instructions and toolchain, while {appName} passes tasks, relevant context and reports between sessions. The coordinator can delegate work and bring the results together.
privacyWebsiteConsentBody: This is a static website hosted on GitHub Pages. We use a cookie to remember the language selected or detected for this browser for one year. We use Google Analytics to understand website visits only with your consent. It uses cookies and sends usage data to Google. If you decline before allowing it, Google Analytics is not loaded. We remember your choice in a cookie for one year. You can change it through “Analytics settings” in the footer of the homepage or privacy page. If you withdraw consent after allowing analytics, we stop sending further analytics data from that page and remove its Google Analytics cookies. GitHub records visitors’ IP addresses for security purposes; see GitHub’s privacy statement.
